claim: For the two-stage second-order SSP-optimal SDIRK method with coefficient matrix \(a_{11}=a_{22}=1/4\), \(a_{21}=1/2\), \(b_1=b_2=1/2\)—equivalently, two consecutive implicit-midpoint steps of length \(h/2\)—endpoint positivity on finite-state continuous-time Markov chains has a sharp dimension boundary. For every two-state generator \(Q\) and every \(h\ge0\), the one-step matrix \(R_h(Q)=[(I+hQ/4)(I-hQ/4)^{-1}]^2\) is entrywise nonnegative and row-stochastic. In contrast, for the three-state pure-birth generator \(Q=[[-1,1,0],[0,-1,1],[0,0,0]]\), the \((1,2)\) entry of \(R_h(Q)\) is \(16h(4-h)/(h+4)^3\), so endpoint positivity holds exactly for \(0\le h\le4\) and fails for every \(h>4\). Thus three states are the smallest dimension in which endpoint positivity can fail, and the classical SSP coefficient \(4\) is already sharp inside three-state Markov generators even though every two-state Markov generator is endpoint-positive for arbitrarily large steps.
integrity: The proof is analytic. A dependency-free exact-rational checker reconstructs the one-step matrices independently and verifies representative formulas and the three-state sign transition; finite checks are corroborative rather than an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns exact-arithmetic endpoint nonnegativity for autonomous finite-state Markov generators under SSP-SDIRK2(2). It does not assert intermediate-stage positivity, floating-point positivity, or results for time-dependent generators. Full text of the most directly relevant Horvath positivity papers was not recovered, leaving a specific residual originality risk.
title: Two-state immunity and three-state sharpness for endpoint positivity of SSP-SDIRK2(2)
